files.content:
Interview with Oma (Geertje van Dam-Boersma), recorded 18 July 2026 at the kitchen table. Interviewer: Thomas (grandson).

THOMAS: Let's start with your father. What do you remember being told about when he was born?

OMA: My father, Hendrik, was born in 1919. I know the register says 1921, everyone waves the register at me, but his own mother told me 1919, at this table, and she would know better than a clerk with cold fingers. The registration was late because of the farm — they registered him when they registered the new calf, that was the joke.

THOMAS: And where was that?

OMA: On the farm at Wons. The family had been at Wons since anyone could count. He left for the harbor town in 1936 to work the fish auction — sixteen years old with one good coat.

THOMAS: When did he meet your mother?

OMA: At the auction. She was a mender of nets, Anna Visser, and he bought a torn net on purpose three weeks running to have a reason to speak to her. They married in 1941. I do not know the church — ask Tante Riet, she has the photograph with the church behind them.

THOMAS: And you came along —

OMA: 1943, in the middle of everything. My brother Jan in 1946, and Els, the youngest, in 1949. Three of us in a house you could cross in four steps.

THOMAS: What about the shop I've heard about?

OMA: The fish shop, 1952 he opened it, the year of the great herring catch. He painted the name himself and misspelled it — VAN DAMM with two Ms — and he refused to repaint it, he said the extra M was free advertising. It stayed two Ms until they sold in 1961.

THOMAS: Did he ever talk about his brothers?

OMA: Two brothers. Willem, the eldest, and little Piet. Piet went to Rotterdam — or Willem went, and Piet stayed — no. I am not sure. One of them went to Rotterdam for the docks and one stayed at Wons. Do not write it down as certain, I am guessing which was which.

THOMAS: Anything you want the record to keep?

OMA: That he sang. Nobody remembers it because he only sang gutting fish, when his hands were busy and his face forgot to be stern. Put that in. The dates you can argue about. The singing was true.

[recording ends 41:19]
